text:
The Jets traded Connor Hellebuyck to New Jersey on Oct. 23, after the three-time Vezina winner asked out and was suspended for not reporting to camp, and the rest of Winnipeg's season will be measured against that deal. So far it's going better than anyone feared. The Jets won six straight before Ottawa ended the streak 2-1 on Tuesday, per Ken Wiebe of the Winnipeg Free Press.

Dawson Mercer, the main piece coming back, has eight points in his last ten games against 5.3 expected, and The Hockey Writers wrote that he's finding his stride with his new team. Mark Scheifele has been making franchise history; Sportsnet wrote that he's rewriting the record books. Kyle Connor reached 700 career points.

The numbers are more sober than the streak. Winnipeg is 10-9-3 with 23 points, about one more than our expected points, and gets 48% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), 47% at five on five. The Scheifele, Connor and Cole Perfetti line has outscored opponents 9-6 at 52%, and Dylan Samberg with Neal Pionk is the most-used pair at about the same level. Both special teams run hot and cold: the power play creates 0.8 expected goals a game, the penalty kill allows 0.83. Our playoff odds are 30%. Scott Arniel's team has steadied, but it still looks like a bubble team.
